title: Temperature - sharpening and flattening a distribution

questions.prompt: What does the temperature parameter do, in one sentence?
options: It divides every logit by T before the softmax, so a smaller T sharpens the distribution and a larger T flattens it
It adds a random number to each logit so the model does not always give the same answer
It truncates the lowest-scoring options so only the top three can be chosen
It scales the model's output layer weights, which changes what the model has learned
questions.explain: Temperature is a divisor applied to the logits before the softmax: p_i(T) = exp(z_i / T) / sum_j exp(z_j / T). T below 1 makes the gaps bigger and the distribution peaked; T above 1 makes them smaller and the distribution flat. The second option describes noise injection, not temperature - randomness comes from sampling, which this repo never does. The third option describes a decoding strategy for text models. The fourth option is wrong because temperature changes no weights; it is a deployment-time dial, not retraining.

questions.prompt: A model's top option sits at 0.63 at T = 1.0 and at 0.98 at T = 0.25. With a threshold of 0.6, what changes between the two?
options: Both the label and the action: the top option changes and the harness starts acting
Neither the label nor the action: the top option stays the same and it already acted at 0.63
Only the action: the top option stays the same, but the harness starts acting at 0.98
Only the label: the top option changes, but the action was already happening
questions.explain: Both numbers are above the 0.6 threshold, so the action (and the label) is the same at both temperatures: temperature changes the probability, not the decision in this case. The third option is the tempting one, but it only holds when the threshold falls between the two probabilities - and here 0.63 already clears 0.6. The fourth option is wrong because temperature can never change which option is on top. The first option is wrong on both counts.

questions.prompt: Why does the temperature never change which option the model ranks first?
options: Because the softmax output is rounded to four decimals
Because dividing every logit by the same positive number cannot reorder them
Because the threshold is applied after the ranking is fixed
Because temperature is only applied to `noul` answers
questions.explain: If z_i > z_j then z_i / T > z_j / T for every T > 0, so every pairwise comparison survives - the argmax, and in fact the whole ranking, is unchanged. The first option is irrelevant: rounding is a presentation step and rounding cannot reorder a set of values either way. The third option is a real property of this repo - the threshold does come after the answer - but it is not why the ranking is invariant; a ranking-invariance argument is. The fourth option is wrong because temperature is a logit-level concept and this repo's example applies it to a three-option choice.

questions.prompt: In a text model, why does a low temperature make the output repetitive?
options: Because sampling picks the top option more often when the distribution is sharp
Because a low temperature disables the tokeniser
Because the model has fewer parameters at a low temperature
questions.explain: Sampling draws the next token at random with probability p_i, so the shape of the distribution controls the randomness: a peaked distribution (low T) lands on the top token almost every time, which reads as repetitive, while a flat distribution (high T) wanders. The second, third and fourth options are unrelated to temperature - a temperature dial changes no weights, no tokeniser and no context window. Note that this repo never samples: it always takes the top option, which is why the OpenAI-compatible adapter sends the API-level "temperature": 0 for greedy decoding.
